turns.text: Lloyd, I'm trying to set up a desktop GUI app using Electron, but it's way too heavy. Do you know any lighter alternatives for JavaScript?
Have you looked into Tauri or Neutralino.js? They use the system's native webview, so they are much smaller than Electron.
I saw Tauri, but I'm not into Rust. I want to stick to JS/TS. What about NodeGui?
NodeGui is a great option if you want Qt bindings in Node. It lets you build native-looking apps with JavaScript.
Right, I remember reading that Atul Ramachandran is the author of NodeGui. He wrote a really clear tutorial on it last year.
Yes, his tutorials are quite popular for getting started with Qt in Node. The documentation is solid too.
Cool. Anyway, my internet went down again. I need to fix that router setting. Do you remember the default gateway IP?
It is usually 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.0.1. Check your command prompt with 'ipconfig' to be sure.
Found it. Thanks. Also, did the package for NodeGui install successfully?
I don't have access to your local terminal, but if you ran 'npm install @nodegui/nodegui', it should be in your node_modules folder now.
